name: rippled cross-dependency review corpus
description: Source-only bug replays and clean controls for evaluating static routing and clustered AI review without depending on live branches.

replay_contract.bug_cases: Start from a tree containing the historical fix, apply only the listed production-code mutation, and retain the fixed regression tests. The resulting PR should be behavior=broken and coverage=covered.
replay_contract.control_cases: Apply only the listed semantics-preserving hunk. The resulting PR should be behavior=correct and coverage=covered.
replay_contract.oracle_isolation: Do not place this manifest, its expected judgement, or its ground-truth prose in the model evidence packet. Use it only after judging.
replay_contract.execution: Build graph, map diff, rank clusters, judge the selected cluster, then compare the structured result with expected_judgement. Each case should run in an isolated worktree or disposable branch.

provenance.subject: fix: bind batch required signers to sfDelegate for delegated inner txns

current_develop.note: Batch.cpp uses rb.getInitiator() and the complete testBatchDelegateConsent regression suite is present; the replay is a one-line production mutation.

steps.instruction: Derive each inner required signer from sfAccount only instead of the inner transaction initiator/sfDelegate. Keep the outer-account elision unchanged. On current code this is the one-line getInitiator() -> getAccountID(sfAccount) mutation.

source_citations.evidence: The fix selects sfDelegate when present before deciding whether the authorizer must appear in sfBatchSigners.

tests.assertion: A delegated inner whose delegate did not sign is rejected; valid delegate co-signing succeeds.

routing.why: The diff touches the Batch wrapper's signer derivation while sfDelegate is an exact PermissionDelegation lever. The pair meets at signature, permission, and initiator forks; clustered review should investigate them once rather than emit three independent verdicts.

provenance.subject: Disallow fee sponsorship on Batch inner txs (#7754)

current_develop.note: The inner isFeeSponsored guard and Sponsor_test inner/outer Batch cases are present; deleting only the two-line guard cleanly replays the bug.

steps.instruction: Remove only the inner-transaction guard that rejects sfSponsor combined with isFeeSponsored(stx). Preserve the outer-Batch sponsorship behavior and all tests.

source_citations.evidence: The fixed preflight rejects fee sponsorship on an inner while leaving fee sponsorship on the outer Batch legal.

tests.assertion: Pre-funded and co-signed fee-sponsored inners are rejected, while an outer fee-sponsored Batch succeeds.

routing.why: The changed wrapper consumes the Sponsor common fields and controls whether inner transactions can reach Sponsor fee-payer logic. This is a direct Batch x Sponsor cluster with both shared-field and fork evidence.

cases.title: TrustSet misroutes a reserve sponsor to the counterparty

current_develop.note: TrustSet.cpp still has getSponsor plus distinct lowSponsor/highSponsor uses, and the counterparty misroute test is present.

steps.instruction: Bypass the per-side getSponsor(account) filter and pass the transaction-level sponsorSle into both low-side and high-side reserve updates. Retain the fixed free-tier condition and regression test so the mutation isolates counterparty sponsor misrouting.

source_citations.evidence: The fix scopes a transaction sponsor to the submitter side before changing owner counts or sfLowSponsor/sfHighSponsor.

tests.assertion: A holder update that trips the issuer-side reserve gate must not attach the holder's sponsor to the issuer side or alter sponsor counts.

routing.why: The changed TrustSet implementation manipulates Sponsor-owned fields and reserve state on a two-sided ledger object. The case tests whether routing carries account-side state into the semantic investigation instead of treating sfSponsor as a generic field match.

cases.title: Sponsored EscrowFinish releases reserve too late

provenance.subject: fix: Sponsored token EscrowFinish falsely rejects net-zero recycling (#7678)

current_develop.note: EscrowFinish.cpp retains the featureSponsor ordering split and both reserve-recycling regression families are present.

steps.instruction: For Sponsor-enabled ledgers, move decreaseOwnerCountForObject back to after token delivery. Preserve the legacy pre-Sponsor ordering and retain the regression tests. The mutation should make a reserve-neutral holding replacement fail because both objects temporarily count at once.

operations.new:
// Adjust source owner count
    decreaseOwnerCountForObject(ctx_.view(), account, slep, 1, ctx_.journal);

source_citations.evidence: Under featureSponsor the fixed implementation releases the escrow reserve before delivery can auto-create a replacement holding.

tests.assertion: The same self-escrow reserve window fails under legacy ordering and succeeds when Sponsor ordering recycles the released slot.

routing.why: The diff has an exact featureSponsor gate inside EscrowFinish and changes ordering around a reserve-sensitive delivery. It tests whether the packet includes state transitions and amendment-on/off behavior, not only shared function names.

cases.title: AMM clawback privilege is blocked by deep freeze

provenance.subject: fix: Allow OverrideFreeze to bypass individual/deep freeze on AMM trust lines (#6959)

current_develop.note: FreezeInvariant.cpp retains the fixOverrideFreeze condition and AMMClawback_test retains the amendment-split deep-freeze assertion; the production hunks can be reversed without touching tests.

steps.instruction: Restore the pre-fix OverrideFreeze condition that requires !isAMMLine or globalFreeze. Keep the helper plumbing unchanged so the mutation isolates the policy predicate, and do not reverse the AMMClawback regression tests.

source_citations.evidence: The cleanup-gated fix allows the AMMClawback OverrideFreeze privilege to bypass individual and deep freeze on AMM trust lines.

tests.assertion: The same deep-frozen AMM clawback fails before Cleanup3_4_0 and succeeds after it.

routing.why: The transactor reaches a privilege invariant whose behavior is also controlled by DeepFreeze state and a cleanup amendment. This deliberately tests routing beyond generic Transactor forks; missing it identifies an invariant-gate extraction gap rather than a judge failure.

cases.title: Name the Sponsor fee-payer predicate without changing it

current_develop.note: getFeePayer still contains the exact inline predicate from the seed base, so the local extraction applies without adaptation.

steps.instruction: Replace the inline sfSponsor && isFeeSponsored(tx) condition with a const bool sponsorPaysFee initialized to that exact expression, then branch on the local. Make no other change.

source_citations.evidence: The extracted local is textually identical to the prior branch condition.

tests.assertion: A sponsored Payment consistently attributes the fee to the sponsor when the sponsee cannot pay it.

routing.why: The generic getFeePayer refactor exposes Sponsor but no pair-specific Payment signal among hundreds of consumers. The exact Payment x Sponsor candidate should remain discoverable, but requiring it inside a small top-K budget would test arbitrary tie-breaking rather than semantic routing. The judge must still avoid turning structural relevance into a false positive when this candidate is selected.

cases.title: Name the Sponsor presence predicate without changing it

provenance.subject: refactor: name sponsor and AMM feature predicates

current_develop.note: checkSponsor still contains the exact inline sfSponsor presence check; only the selected Transactor hunk is needed.

steps.instruction: Apply only the Transactor.cpp hunk: bind tx.isFieldPresent(sfSponsor) to const bool hasSponsor and negate that local in the early return. Do not include the unrelated AMMVote hunk from the seed commit.

source_citations.evidence: The named local contains the exact pre-refactor sponsor-presence expression.

tests.assertion: Reserve sponsorship remains blocked when permission delegation is also present.

routing.why: Sponsor and PermissionDelegation are both mediators of checkSponsor. The control verifies that clustering does not equate a high-signal amendment intersection with broken behavior.
